title: Move as One
aim: Serve and return from a stack (both partners start on the same half) and slide to your preferred sides as one team, without leaving a gap in the middle.

stages.title: Serve and Slide
stages.inShort: A serves, then A and B slide to their favourite sides as one team. No opponents needed, just the movement.
rules: Before you start, agree as a team who plays the left side and who plays the right side.
A serves from the side the score says. B stands on the same half, next to A. That is stacking: both start on one side so you can end up on the sides you prefer.
Right after the serve, A slides across to their side. B holds or slides to theirs.
10 serves from one side, then switch sides. Aim for at least 8 clean slides out of 10.
Mix even and odd scores, so you practise the slide from both starting sides.
stages.tooEasy: Bring in two players to return: they hit short and aggressive returns, so the slide has to be quicker. Even harder: A serves shorter, so the return comes back faster.
stages.tooHard: Stay on one score (even) until the slide feels natural, then add the odd score.
stages.goodLooksLike: Both of you end up on your side without thinking about it, and you are ready for the next ball.

drill.title: Serve & Slide – Stack Mechanics, Serving Side

stages.title: Return and Switch
stages.inShort: B returns straight down the line, then you try both ways to reach your sides: crossing on the court, or A stepping on from outside.
rules: No opponents: start each rep with a feed (a soft, straight ball put into play from the other side instead of a real serve).
Before every return, B gives a hand signal. A confirms out loud.
Round 1, on-court: both start on the court. B returns down the line (straight ahead, along the sideline), then crosses to their side. A covers the middle while B crosses.
Round 2, off-court: A waits outside the court on the side A will play. B returns and goes straight to their side, no crossing.
10 returns per round, then swap who returns. At the end, pick the way that suits your team.
stages.tooEasy: Play it with a serving team on the other side: they mix the pace and angle of the serve, and B still returns down the line and stacks. Even harder: a return only counts if it lands in the back quarter of the court.
stages.tooHard: Practise one way at a time: stay with Round 2 (no crossing) until the signal and the step-on work, then add Round 1.
stages.goodLooksLike: Every return goes down the line, the signal comes every time, and the middle is never empty while B crosses.

stages.title: Catch Them Crossing
stages.inShort: Four players: the return team stacks and switches, and the serving team attacks the player who is still crossing.
stages.onlyTwo: Play Drill 2 again: a return only counts if it lands in the back quarter of the court.
rules: Four players, two teams: one team serves, the other team returns.
The return team stacks on the court and switches after the return, as in Stage 2, Round 1. Before every serve, they call the switch out loud.
After the return, the serving team plays the next ball quickly at the crossing player, best at the hip or shoulder while that player is still moving.
Goal for the serving team: the crossing player cannot block or reset cleanly (send a soft ball back that takes the pace off).
Play 10 points, then the teams swap: servers return, returners serve.
stages.tooEasy: No call any more: the return team only shows a hand signal (open hand = switch), and the serving team has to read it and decide. Even harder: the return team may fake the switch, and the attack must come within the first two shots after the return.
stages.tooHard: Keep the switch called out loud, and the serving team may wait for a good ball instead of attacking at once.
stages.goodLooksLike: The serving team sees the switch coming and hits at the moving player, and the return team still gets to its sides as one.

drill.title: Stack Unwind Attack – Attacking the Crossing Opponent as the Serving Team
